say.text: Salah ad-Din's power was now on a solid footing, and his authority consolidated. He acted as the lieutenant of Nur ad-Din, and had the khutba said in Nur ad-Din's name in all the cities of Egypt.
When Nur ad-Din wrote, he addressed him as 'the emir isfahsalar', the emir who commands the army, and signed his letters with a mark, so as not to compromise the dignity of his name.
From then on Salah ad-Din renounced wine and the pleasures of his youth, and gave himself up to the work of government.
They have come, my lord. Three of four. That is more than most men are given.
I did not win them. You did, one at a time, by telling each what he could hear.
Then do not make me repeat it. A lord is judged by what he does with what he is given.
